The Chinese item name identifies Poké Ball; Unicode é replaces the reserved at-sign glyph spelling. Full-text review: Abbreviates Poké Ball for the seven-cell Bag-list field.
This payload is shared by the victory and defeat paths; a neutral heading introduces the separate dynamic money line without duplicating or falsely attributing the result.

The Chinese source contains only the connective But; the old witness's added claim that a move cannot be learned belongs to subsequent composed fragments and is omitted.
Directly preserves the Chinese question about forgetting another move; older is not stated by the source.

Corrects the old Forget action: this fragment asks whether to give up learning the new move; the trailing space is structural because the move name and separate question suffix follow at runtime. Full-text review: Splits the complete learning-cancel question at a word boundary so its move name and final question mark remain inside the two-row battle window.

Announces the opponent's next Pokémon in the natural Generation I battle voice; the trailing space joins its dynamic species name. Full-text review: Places the upcoming Pokémon name alone on the second row.
